\section*{AP \({ }^{\text {® }}\) CALCULUS AB \\ 2002 SCORING GUIDELINES (Form B)}

\section*{Question 2}

The number of gallons, \(P(t)\), of a pollutant in a lake changes at the rate \(P^{\prime}(t)=1-3 e^{-0.2 \sqrt{t}}\) gallons per day, where \(t\) is measured in days. There are 50 gallons of the pollutant in the lake at time \(t=0\). The lake is considered to be safe when it contains 40 gallons or less of pollutant.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Is the amount of pollutant increasing at time \(t=9\) ? Why or why not?
\item[(b)] For what value of \(t\) will the number of gallons of pollutant be at its minimum? Justify your answer.
\item[(c)] Is the lake safe when the number of gallons of pollutant is at its minimum? Justify your answer.
\item[(d)] An investigator uses the tangent line approximation to \(P(t)\) at \(t=0\) as a model for the amount of pollutant in the lake. At what time \(t\) does this model predict that the lake becomes safe?
\item[(a)] \(P^{\prime}(9)=1-3 e^{-0.6}=-0.646<0\)
so the amount is not increasing at this time.
\item[(b)] \(P^{\prime}(t)=1-3 e^{-0.2 \sqrt{t}}=0\)
\(t=(5 \ln 3)^{2}=30.174\)
\(P^{\prime}(t)\) is negative for \(0<t<(5 \ln 3)^{2}\) and positive for \(t>(5 \ln 3)^{2}\). Therefore there is a minimum at \(t=(5 \ln 3)^{2}\).
\item[(c)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
P(30.174) & =50+\int_{0}^{30.174}\left(1-3 e^{-0.2 \sqrt{t}}\right) d t \\
& =35.104<40, \text { so the lake is safe. }
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(d)] \(P^{\prime}(0)=1-3=-2\). The lake will become safe when the amount decreases by 10. A linear model predicts this will happen when \(t=5\).
\item[1] : answer with reason
\(3\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { sets } P^{\prime}(t)=0 \\ 1: \text { solves for } t \\ 1: \text { justification }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(3\left\{\begin{aligned} 1: \text { integrand } \\ 1: \text { limits } \\ 1: \text { conclusion with reason } \\ \quad \text { based on integral of } P^{\prime}(t)\end{aligned}\right.\)
\(2\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { slope of tangent line } \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\end{itemize}
